chapters.title: Chapter 1: ITR Basics: What, Why and Who Must File

lessons.title: Why File Even When It Is Not Mandatory: Refunds, Loans, Visas and Loss Carry-Forward

children.text: In the last lesson you learnt the tests that make filing compulsory. Plenty of people clear all of them and conclude they can skip the return. Legally, they can. Financially, it is often a mistake. An ITR is not just a compliance form. It is a refund claim, a tax shield for future years, and the most widely accepted proof of income in India.

stats.label: Refund Interest
stats.context: From 1 April, if you file by the due date

stats.label: Capital Losses
stats.context: Carried forward only if you file on time

stats.label: Income Proof
stats.context: Commonly asked for by lenders and visa offices

children.text: Reason 1: The Only Way to Get Your TDS Back

Banks, employers, tenants, mutual funds and companies paying dividends deduct TDS based on simple thresholds. They do not know your full income. So when your actual tax is lower than the TDS, the extra money sits with the government against your PAN. No one will send it back automatically. The ITR is the claim.

Common situations where this happens: FD interest above the bank's TDS threshold for a retiree with little other income, TDS on salary deducted for a part-year job, dividend TDS on shares held in a Zerodha or Groww demat, TDS on rent from a tenant, or TDS on a property sale. If your tax works out to less than what was deducted, a refund is waiting.
The Government Pays You Interest, If You Are on Time

markDefs.definition: Simple interest the Income Tax Department pays on a refund, at 0.5% for every month or part of a month, calculated under Section 437 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 244A of the 1961 Act).

children.text: Refunds come with
interest on refund

under Section 437 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 244A of the Income-tax Act, 1961). The rate is 0.5% per month or part of a month. For a refund of TDS or advance tax, interest runs from 1 April of the assessment year if you file by the due date, but only from the date of filing if you file late. No interest is paid if the refund is less than 10% of the tax determined on processing. The interest you receive is itself taxable as income from other sources in the year you get it.

body.latex: \text{Refund Interest} = \text{Refund} \times 0.5\% \times \text{Number of Months (part month counts as full)}
body.caption: Simple interest, not compounded. The period ends on the date the refund is granted.

body.title: Calculate the Refund Interest
body.prompt: Pooja, a retired school principal in Lucknow, is not required to file for FY 2025-26, but has ₹20,000 of excess TDS on her FD interest. Her tax payable works out to nil. She files on 25 July 2026, before the due date, and the refund is credited to her bank account on 20 September 2026. How much interest does the department pay her?
body.explanation: She filed by the due date, so interest runs from 1 April 2026. April, May, June, July and August are five full months, and September is a part month, which counts as a full month. That is 6 months. ₹20,000 × 0.5% × 6 = ₹600. Her tax determined is nil, so the refund easily clears the 10% condition. She will report the ₹600 as income from other sources for FY 2026-27, the year she received it.

children.text: Reason 2: Carrying Losses Forward to Cut Future Tax

This is the reason that matters most for anyone who invests or trades. A bad year in the market can reduce your tax in a good year, but only if the loss is on record. And the law is strict about how it gets on record: most losses can be carried forward only if you file the return for the loss year by the original due date. A belated return, filed even one day after the due date, forfeits the carry-forward. This condition comes from Section 80 of the 1961 Act, read with Section 139(3), and continues under the 2025 Act.

body.caption: How Common Losses Are Carried Forward
headers: Can Be Set Off in Future Years Against

cells: Short-term capital loss, e.g. shares sold within 12 months
Non-speculative business loss, including F&O trading losses
Speculative business loss, e.g. intraday equity trading
No, allowed even on a belated return

children.text: Worked Example: What One Return Is Worth

Rohit, 24, works at a startup in Noida on a salary of ₹4,50,000 and trades on Zerodha. In FY 2025-26, his salary after the standard deduction is ₹3,75,000, below the ₹4 lakh limit, and he books a short-term capital loss of ₹80,000 on small-cap stocks. He is not required to file. In FY 2026-27 he moves to a new job at ₹18,00,000 and books a short-term gain of ₹1,00,000 on listed shares, taxed at 20% plus 4% cess.

body.caption: Rohit's Short-Term Gain Tax in FY 2026-27

body.title: Tax on Rohit's ₹1 Lakh Short-Term Gain

body.text: A free, non-mandatory return filed in July 2026 saved Rohit ₹16,640 a year later. Losses you do not report are losses you cannot use.

Capital losses and F&O losses mean ITR-2 or ITR-3, not ITR-1. Filing ITR-1 and simply leaving the loss out does not carry anything forward. Also, an updated return filed later cannot be used to report a loss or increase one, so the original due date really is the deadline for losses.

body.title: What Does Filing Late Cost You?
body.question: Sameer is not required to file, but files a belated return for FY 2025-26 in October 2026. Which of these does he lose by missing the 31 July 2026 due date?
options: The right to claim his excess TDS as a refund
The right to carry forward his ₹50,000 short-term capital loss
The ability to use the ITR acknowledgement as proof of income
The right to carry forward a loss from his let-out flat
body.explanation: A belated return still gets his TDS refunded (though interest only runs from the date of filing) and still works as income proof. A house property loss can be carried forward even on a belated return. But a short-term capital loss can only be carried forward if the return is filed by the due date, so that benefit is gone.

body.title: Lock In the Rule
body.textWithBlank: A speculative loss from intraday equity trading can be carried forward for ___ years, and only against speculative income.
body.explanation: Speculative business losses carry forward for 4 years. Capital losses and non-speculative business losses, including F&O losses, carry forward for 8 years.

children.text: Reason 3: Loans, Credit Cards and Insurance

Lenders like SBI, HDFC Bank and Bajaj Finance need proof that your income is real and stable. For salaried applicants, salary slips and Form 16 often do the job, but ITRs strengthen the file. For freelancers, consultants, shop owners and gig workers, ITR acknowledgements for the last two or three years are usually the core document. No ITRs often means a smaller loan, a higher rate, or a rejection. High-cover term insurance plans and premium credit cards also commonly ask for income proof in the form of ITRs.

body.title: Applying for a ₹40 Lakh Home Loan as a Freelancer

columns.label: Three Years of ITRs Filed
points: Income is documented and verifiable against Form 26AS and AIS
Lender can assess eligibility on declared income
Rising declared income over three years supports a larger loan
Faster processing with fewer additional documents

columns.label: No ITRs Filed
points: Bank statements alone rarely satisfy underwriting
Income may be treated as unverifiable
Likely rejection or a much smaller sanctioned amount
Filing three years at once later looks exactly like what it is

children.text: Reason 4: Visas and Moving Abroad

Visa applications for Schengen countries, the UK, Canada and Australia commonly ask for ITR acknowledgements for the last two or three years as evidence of financial standing and ties to India. Requirements vary by country and visa type, and change often, but a consistent filing history makes your application stronger. The same goes for students whose parents are sponsoring study abroad: the sponsor's ITRs are frequently requested.

body.text: Myth check: you may have heard that non-filers pay TDS at double the rate. That rule, under Sections 206AB and 206CCA of the 1961 Act, was removed with effect from 1 April 2025. Higher TDS still applies if you have not furnished a valid PAN, so keep your PAN linked to Aadhaar. The reasons to file are about what you gain, not a penalty rate.

body.label: Late Fee for Voluntary Filers
body.value: Generally nil if you were not required to file
body.context: The late fee applies to people who were required to file. If your income is below the basic exemption limit and you crossed no trigger, a belated return usually attracts no fee, but you still lose on-time benefits like loss carry-forward.

body.title: The Freelancer Who Thinks Filing Is Pointless
body.scenario: Ayesha, 26, is a freelance illustrator in Kochi. For FY 2025-26, her income after expenses is ₹3,60,000. Two clients deducted a total of ₹9,000 TDS under the professional fees provisions. She crosses no high-value trigger. She plans to apply for a France tourist visa in 2027 and hopes to buy a flat with a home loan in about three years. She says filing is a waste of time since she owes no tax.
body.prompt: Give Ayesha three concrete reasons to file for FY 2025-26, and tell her by when she should do it.
body.modelAnswer: First, the refund: her income of ₹3,60,000 is below the ₹4,00,000 new regime basic exemption limit, so her tax is nil and the full ₹9,000 TDS is refundable, but only through an ITR. Filing by the due date also earns her interest from 1 April 2026. Second, the visa: a France tourist visa is a Schengen visa, and applications commonly ask for recent ITR acknowledgements as proof of income, so a 2027 application benefits from returns filed for FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-27. Third, the home loan: as a freelancer, her ITRs will be the main proof of income a lender relies on, and starting a three-year track record now means she will have one when she applies. For presumptive professional income she would typically use ITR-4, or ITR-3 if she keeps regular books. She should file by the due date for her form, which she should confirm on the portal, as business and professional returns can carry a later date than ITR-1 and ITR-2. Filing by 31 July 2026 is safe either way.

children.text: Proof of income when claiming compensation, for example in motor accident claims, where courts rely on declared income
Documented source of funds if you later make a large purchase, such as property or a big investment, and the department asks where the money came from
Eligibility documents for government contracts, tenders and some business registrations
A clean habit: someone who files every year is far less likely to miss the year it actually becomes mandatory

body.title: Should You File Even If You Don't Have To?
steps: Open Form 26AS and check whether any TDS or TCS was deducted against your PAN for FY 2025-26
Check your Zerodha, Groww or other broker's tax P&L report for any capital losses booked in the year
Check for F&O or intraday trading losses, which need ITR-3
Think ahead: are you likely to apply for a loan, credit card or visa in the next three years?
If any answer is yes, plan to file before 31 July 2026 rather than after it

points: Excess TDS is only refunded when you file, and filing by the due date earns interest at 0.5% per month from 1 April under Section 437 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 244A of the 1961 Act)
Capital losses and F&O losses carry forward for 8 years and speculative losses for 4 years, but only if the return for the loss year is filed by the original due date
House property losses are the exception and can be carried forward even on a belated return
An unreported ₹80,000 short-term capital loss can cost over ₹16,000 in extra tax the following year
Lenders, visa offices and insurers commonly ask for two to three years of ITRs, especially from freelancers and the self-employed
The higher TDS rate for non-filers under Sections 206AB and 206CCA was removed from 1 April 2025, so file for the benefits, not out of fear of that rule
